questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With One Pivot
questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-x-y-3z=1 \\ 2x+2y+6z=-2 \\ -2x-2y-6z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a 3x3 System That Is Not in Row Echelon Form
questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-3y=1 \\  & y+2z=1 \\  & 5x-7y+17z=7\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -7 & 17 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -7 & 17 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 8 & 17 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-8){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 40 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 13 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With Two Pivots
questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x-3y+6z=9 \\ -x+4z=4 \\ x+y-2z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 & 6 & 9 \\ -1 & 0 & 4 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 & 6 & 9 \\ -1 & 0 & 4 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 4 & 4 \\ -3 & -3 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & -3 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-4z=-4 \\ y+2z=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4z-4 \\ y=1-2z \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4z-4 \\ 1-2z \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-1 \\ 2x-5y-3z=6 \\ -x+2y=1\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 & 6 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ into reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 & 6 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 8 \\ -1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & -17 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+6z=-17 \\ y+3z=-8 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation, we can remove this equation from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-6z-17 \\ y=-3z-8 \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-6z-17 \\ -3z-8 \\ z\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
